bug_description.original: A use after free vulnerability exists in gpg, specifically in g10/mainproc.c within the proc_plaintext function, where freed memory is accessed.
bug_description.normalized: A use after free vulnerability exists in gpg, specifically in g10/mainproc.c within the proc_plaintext function, where freed memory is accessed.

source.description: The OpenPGP plaintext-packet parser reads the attacker-controlled filename length byte from the input stream into namelen.

sink.description: proc_plaintext reads pt->namelen after pkt->pkt.plaintext has already been freed through free_packet.

root_cause.description: The plaintext packet is freed before proc_plaintext finishes copying metadata from the PKT_plaintext object into the plaintext marker.

taint_source.description: Untrusted fuzz bytes are written to a temporary file and then passed to normal GnuPG signature verification; the harness is an unscored boundary.

tainted_value_origin.description: First vulnerability-relevant value: the parser reads the attacker-controlled literal filename length from the packet input stream.

root_cause_analysis.summary: The attacker-controlled OpenPGP plaintext packet is parsed into a PKT_plaintext object. proc_plaintext keeps a local alias pt to pkt->pkt.plaintext, calls free_packet(pkt, NULL), and then continues to read pt->namelen while constructing the marker control packet. Because free_packet releases the PKT_plaintext object, the later read through pt is a heap-use-after-free.
root_cause_analysis.why_patch_works: The developer patch moves free_packet(pkt, NULL) until after the code copies pt->namelen, pt->mode, pt->timestamp, and pt->name into extrahash. This preserves the lifetime of the PKT_plaintext object for all remaining reads and removes the ASan heap-use-after-free under the same PoC.
